newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Aussie keeps nerve amid rate scare.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Aussie keeps nerve amid rate scare.

text.p: The Australian dollar managed a moderate bounce past US$0.7610 resistance offshore courtesy of short covering by bears frustrated by support at US$0.7550.

The currency even put a brave face on rumours the Reserve Bank was set to cut rates this morning following its monthly board meeting Tuesday, which saw it wobble in London time only to recover in New York.

Most analysts reckon it is too soon after the last easing on May 23 for a move, but given three of the bank's four cuts have been a surprise, nothing could be ruled out. That should keep things tense ahead of the RBA's 9.30 am (2330 GMT) time slot.
By 8.00 am (2200 GMT) the dollar was showing a little of that strain having edged back to US$0.7609/14 from a US$0.7630 high, but was still up on Tuesday's late US$0.7595/00.
Analysts said the clearance of US$0.7610 had patched up some of the technical damage by Monday's slide to a US$0.7560 low and should give the currency an upward bias short term.
But it would need to cut stiff resistance at US$0.7680 -- the high hit last week before weak retail sales data ruined everything -- to signal a bottom had been found.
A slip below 76 cents would suggest the downtrend was far from over and another test of US$0.7550 was brewing.
All talk of levels would be academic should the RBA cut official rates once again, and overnight action in the futures market suggested some thought it a real possibility.

The June 90-day bank bill contract gained seven basis points to 94.65, implying a rate of 5.35 percent against the present 5.50 percent. This contract expires in just eight days time so somebody was certainly afraid of an imminent move.

Analysts said the RBA would have been concerned by the shock slide in April retail sales and the softening in investment intentions for 1997/98 revealed in the Q1 CAPEX data, and might think further insurance was needed and relatively riskless.

Today's GDP data were also set to confirm annual growth slowed sharply in Q1. Median forecasts are for a reasonable quarterly rise of 0.8 percent, but that would still see annual growth slow to 2.2 percent from 3.1 percent in Q4.
And estimates range as low as 0.25 percent which would give yr-yr growth of just 1.75 percent.

But there were also reasons for the RBA to wait, including the weakness of the dollar itself. The currency has sunk two cents since the May 23 easing and stands at 58.0 in trade weighted terms whereas the budget forecasts of low inflation were based on a TWI of 60.0. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
